faq.a: Yes. OpenMW is a new engine and contains no game content, so it runs on the data from your own copy of Morrowind.
Most content mods made for the original game work. Mods that need MWSE, MGE XE or MCP do not, because those patch the original executable that OpenMW replaces.
It is below version 1.0, which the project reserves for full parity with the original engine. The game is fully playable now, with a few remaining gaps such as some AI behaviour.

RuneLite is a widely used third-party client that plays on the official servers with your normal account. Jagex's own rules decide which clients and plugins are permitted, so check them if you are unsure about a particular plugin.
No. RuneLite is free and open source. Old School RuneScape's own membership is separate and optional.

faq.q: How many players can join a map?
faq.a: Up to 128 on a server.

faq.q: Can I play with people on the original Enemy Territory?
faq.a: Yes. ET: Legacy is built to be fully compatible with Enemy Territory 2.60b, so it joins the same servers.
Windows, Linux and macOS.

faq.q: Can friends build in my park?

OpenRCT2 itself is free and open source. Only the original game data has to come from a copy you own.

faq.q: Do I need to buy Doom?
faq.a: No. This edition uses Freedoom, free replacement game content, so nothing needs buying.

faq.q: Can I play mods with it?
faq.a: Yes. GZDoom is the source port that many of the most ambitious Doom mods are built for.

faq.q: Is it good for online play?
faq.a: For online matches, the Zandronum edition is the better choice. GZDoom is best for single-player and mods.
Zandronum supports up to 64 players on a server.
Co-op, deathmatch, team deathmatch, capture the flag, invasion, Last Man Standing, survival and more, with modifiers such as Instagib.

faq.q: Do we need to buy Doom?

faq.q: Can we play the main story together?
faq.a: Yes. Players, NPCs, the world and quests are kept in sync, and the project calls it fully playable. Most remaining problems involve AI.
Yes. PlayBound can run a party server and keep your world saved between sessions.

faq.q: How is it different from VoxeLibre?
faq.a: Mineclonia forked from VoxeLibre in 2023 to focus on stability, multiplayer performance and matching Minecraft's behaviour closely, including redstone, mob AI and a deeper Overworld.
It is in beta. It is playable but not feature-complete, and an update can break an existing world, so keep backups.

faq.a: Yes, at least one of the original games: Shadow of Chernobyl, Clear Sky or Call of Pripyat.
